packet.headline_seed: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in the biggest foreign IPO in US history, is urged to build new US fabs
packet.description_seed: The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. Now SK Hynix and Samsung are being asked to build US factories.

what: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in the biggest foreign IPO in US history, is urged to build new US fabs

clean_source_blocks.text: The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. Now SK Hynix and Samsung are being asked to build US factories.

The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. SK Hynix, a South Korean memory chip giant, said Friday it has raised $26.5 billion (KRW 40 trillion) in its US market debut. SK Hynix sold 177.9 million American depositary shares (ADRs) at $149 each, structured so US investors can buy in at roughly a tenth of what a full share costs in Seoul. This deal, the largest-ever US debut by a non-American company, topped Alibaba’s $25 billion IPO in 2014. ---

Top executives from SK Hynix including Chairman Chairman Chey Tae-won, Executive Vice Chairman Chey Jae-won, and CEO Kwak Noh-Jung attended NASDAQ's opening bell ceremony in Times Square this morning to commemorate the listing. SK Hynix, which recently passed Samsung to become South Korea's most valuable company, plans to use the funds to finance the construction of new manufacturing facilities, and to fill them with equipment. As you are no doubt familiar with by now, the AI era is in full swing and it's reshaping the entire technology landscape. Big Tech is pumping money into the sector at an unimaginable rate, and hardware manufacturers are struggling to meet demand. The easy answer is to simply build more factories to boost production but that takes both time and money.

Editor's take: A foreign company choosing to list in the US at a premium rather than a discount, with orders covering seven times the shares on offer, is the clearest signal yet that American investors are willing to pay up for direct exposure to the AI memory supply chain rather than route around it through Samsung or Micron alone. US equity markets are open for a full session today; SK Hynix ADR prices above are intraday indications and can change materially through the close. original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch]
The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. SK Hynix, a South Korean memory chip giant, said Friday it has raised $26.5 billion (KRW 40 trillion) in its US market debut.

SK Hynix sold 177.9 million American depositary shares (ADRs) at $149 each, structured so US investors can buy in at roughly a tenth of what a full share costs in Seoul. This deal, the largest-ever US debut by a non-American company, topped Alibaba’s $25 billion IPO in 2014.

---

[Lähde: TechSpot]
What just happened? SK Hynix debuted on the NASDAQ stock market on Friday following an investor roadshow that saw stops in Asia, Europe, and the US. The South Korean semiconductor manufacturing company priced its American Depositary Receipts at $149 per, resulting in a haul of roughly $26.5 billion.

According to the BBC, it's the largest ever listing by a foreign company in the US.

One source familiar with the matter told Reuters that demand for SK Hynix shares was more than seven times higher than the number of shares available. SK Hynix hasn't commented on demand or pricing as of this writing, however, and the source wasn't identified as key details of the sale are confidential.

Top executives from SK Hynix including Chairman Chairman Chey Tae-won, Executive Vice Chairman Chey Jae-won, and CEO Kwak Noh-Jung attended NASDAQ's opening bell ceremony in Times Square this morning to commemorate the listing.

SK Hynix, which recently passed Samsung to become South Korea's most valuable company, plans to use the funds to finance the construction of new manufacturing facilities, and to fill them with equipment.

As you are no doubt familiar with by now, the AI era is in full swing and it's reshaping the entire technology landscape. Big Tech is pumping money into the sector at an unimaginable rate, and hardware manufacturers are struggling to meet demand. The easy answer is to simply build more factories to boost production but that takes both time and money.

The inventory shortage has more or less allowed suppliers to name their price for key components like memory, forcing data centers and device makers to either pay the premium or go without – and that is assuming they are even offered the opportunity to buy at all (big companies get priority on available inventory). For the average consumer, it boils down to more expensive electronics that can sometimes be less capable than what you're used to.

As of this writing, SK Hynix shares are trading at $172.20 on the NASDAQ.

SK Hynix began trading on the Nasdaq Friday after completing the largest ever US share sale by a foreign company. Yahoo Finance reported that the South Korean memory chipmaker priced 177.9 million American depositary receipts at $149 each, raising about $26.5 billion and surpassing the $25 billion Alibaba raised in its 2014 US listing. Each ADR represents one tenth of a common share traded in Seoul, and trading opened Friday under the provisional ticker SKHYV, with the permanent ticker SKHY taking effect Monday.

Bloomberg reported that premarket price indications showed the ADRs trading around $175 each, about 17 percent above the offering price, as of late morning Friday in New York. Orders during the book building process reportedly covered seven times the number of ADRs on offer, with demand coming from global long only funds, technology focused funds, sovereign wealth funds and Asia focused investors.

SK Hynix said it plans to use the proceeds to expand manufacturing capacity in South Korea, including a new fabrication plant at its Yongin semiconductor cluster and an advanced packaging plant in Cheongju, along with purchases of extreme ultraviolet lithography equipment. The company holds a 56.4 percent share of the high bandwidth memory market used in AI processors, ahead of Samsung Electronics and Micron, and crossed a $1 trillion market capitalization for the first time in May as demand for HBM chips tightened supply across the industry.

payload.title: SK Hynix keräsi Yhdysvaltain-listautumisellaan ennätykselliset 26,5 miljardia dollaria
payload.summary: Eteläkorealaisen muistipiirivalmistajan listautuminen ohitti Alibaban aiemman ennätyksen. SK Hynix aikoo käyttää varoja uusien tuotantolaitosten rakentamiseen ja varustamiseen.
payload.content:
Eteläkorealainen muistipiirivalmistaja SK Hynix kertoi perjantaina keränneensä Yhdysvaltain-markkinoille tekemässään listautumisessa 26,5 miljardia dollaria eli noin 40 biljoonaa Etelä-Korean wonia. Järjestely on suurin Yhdysvalloissa toteutettu listautumisanti, jonka takana on maan ulkopuolinen yhtiö, ja se nosti tekoälypiirien kysynnän vauhdittaman muistipiirivalmistajan Wall Streetin huomion kohteeksi.

SK Hynix myi 177,9 miljoonaa amerikkalaista talletustodistusta 149 dollarin kappalehintaan. ADR-talletustodistusten avulla yhdysvaltalaiset sijoittajat voivat käydä kauppaa ulkomaisen yhtiön osakkeisiin sidotuilla arvopapereilla. SK Hynixin järjestelyssä yhden talletustodistuksen hinta vastaa suunnilleen kymmenesosaa siitä, mitä kokonainen yhtiön osake maksaa Soulin pörssissä.

Alibaban ennätys jäi historiaan

Listautumisen koko ylitti kiinalaisen verkkokauppayhtiö Alibaban vuonna 2014 järjestämän 25 miljardin dollarin listautumisannin. SK Hynixin arvopapereihin kohdistui lisäksi huomattavasti tarjontaa suurempi kysyntä: sijoittajien tekemät tilaukset kattoivat tarjolla olleet talletustodistukset seitsenkertaisesti. Kysyntä kuvastaa sijoittajien kiinnostusta suoraan omistukseen tekoälyjärjestelmien muistipiirejä toimittavassa yhtiössä.

Yhtiön johto juhlisti listautumista Nasdaqin avauskellotilaisuudessa New Yorkin Times Squarella. Tilaisuuteen osallistuivat SK Hynixin hallituksen puheenjohtaja Chey Tae-won, varapuheenjohtaja Chey Jae-won ja toimitusjohtaja Kwak Noh-jung. SK Hynix on myös hiljattain ohittanut Samsungin ja noussut Etelä-Korean markkina-arvoltaan suurimmaksi yhtiöksi.

Varat suunnataan tuotantokapasiteettiin

SK Hynix aikoo käyttää listautumisesta saamiaan varoja uusien tuotantolaitosten rakentamiseen ja tehtaissa tarvittavien laitteiden hankkimiseen. Aineistossa ei täsmennetä laitosten sijaintia tai investointien aikataulua. Uuden puolijohdetuotannon käynnistäminen vaatii sekä paljon pääomaa että aikaa, joten listautuminen antaa yhtiölle lisää rahoitusta kapasiteetin kasvattamiseen.

Investointien taustalla on tekoälyjärjestelmien lisäämä muistipiirien kysyntä. Suuret teknologiayhtiöt suuntaavat rahaa tekoälyinfrastruktuuriin, ja laitevalmistajilla on vaikeuksia vastata kasvavaan tarpeeseen nykyisellä tuotannolla. Uusien tehtaiden rakentaminen on suoraviivainen tapa lisätä valmistuskapasiteettia, mutta tuotanto ei kasva välittömästi. Ensimmäisen kaupankäyntipäivän ADR-hinnat olivat vielä päivänsisäisiä tietoja ja saattoivat muuttua ennen Yhdysvaltain osakemarkkinoiden sulkeutumista.

Listautuminen ylitti Alibaban vuonna 2014 tekemän 25 miljardin dollarin ennätyksen.
Yhtiö aikoo käyttää varoja uusien tuotantolaitosten rakentamiseen ja varustamiseen.

article.source_text:
The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. Now SK Hynix and Samsung are being asked to build US factories.

The AI chip boom just produced its biggest Wall Street moment yet. SK Hynix, a South Korean memory chip giant, said Friday it has raised $26.5 billion (KRW 40 trillion) in its US market debut. SK Hynix sold 177.9 million American depositary shares (ADRs) at $149 each, structured so US investors can buy in at roughly a tenth of what a full share costs in Seoul. This deal, the largest-ever US debut by a non-American company, topped Alibaba’s $25 billion IPO in 2014. ---

Top executives from SK Hynix including Chairman Chairman Chey Tae-won, Executive Vice Chairman Chey Jae-won, and CEO Kwak Noh-Jung attended NASDAQ's opening bell ceremony in Times Square this morning to commemorate the listing. SK Hynix, which recently passed Samsung to become South Korea's most valuable company, plans to use the funds to finance the construction of new manufacturing facilities, and to fill them with equipment. As you are no doubt familiar with by now, the AI era is in full swing and it's reshaping the entire technology landscape. Big Tech is pumping money into the sector at an unimaginable rate, and hardware manufacturers are struggling to meet demand. The easy answer is to simply build more factories to boost production but that takes both time and money.

Editor's take: A foreign company choosing to list in the US at a premium rather than a discount, with orders covering seven times the shares on offer, is the clearest signal yet that American investors are willing to pay up for direct exposure to the AI memory supply chain rather than route around it through Samsung or Micron alone. US equity markets are open for a full session today; SK Hynix ADR prices above are intraday indications and can change materially through the close.
